theme: Background refresh: scheduling work and stopping on time

terms.definition: The system service where your app asks for time to run background work later.
terms.example: Register the refresh task with BGTaskScheduler at launch.
terms.code:
import BackgroundTasks
let id = "com.example.refresh"
BGTaskScheduler.shared.register(
    forTaskWithIdentifier: id,
    using: nil) { _ in }

terms.definition: A short background task that lets your app fetch fresh data while it is not on screen.
terms.example: The BGAppRefreshTask updates the feed overnight.

terms.definition: A block of code that the system calls when time is almost up, so you can stop work cleanly.

Learn to explain how an app asks the system for background time to refresh data: BGTaskScheduler, BGAppRefreshTask & Expiration Handler, with real code, a quiz at the end and each example read twice (normal, then slow).

Today's terms
BGTaskScheduler - The system service where your app asks for time to run background work later.
BGAppRefreshTask - A short background task that lets your app fetch fresh data while it is not on screen.
Expiration Handler - A block of code that the system calls when time is almost up, so you can stop work cleanly.

landscape.hook: Can you explain BGTaskScheduler, BGAppRefreshTask and Expiration Handler in English?

dialogue.title: Fresh data while you sleep
dialogue.setting: Refreshing the feed in the background

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Jake, users want the feed to be fresh when they open the app in the morning.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Ask for background time. BGTaskScheduler is the system service for that.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: So the BGTaskScheduler runs my code later?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Yes, when the system decides. In our code, `submit` sends the request.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: What kind of work do we schedule?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: A BGAppRefreshTask. It is short, and it fetches fresh data while the app is off screen.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Can I choose the exact time?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: No. The system picks the time, so never promise one to the user.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: What if my download takes too long?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Set an expiration handler. The system calls it when time is almost up.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: So the expiration handler cancels the download, like `stop` in our code?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Yes. Stop cleanly in the expiration handler, then finish the BGAppRefreshTask.
